description_full: InterDigital, Inc. operates as a global research and development company focuses on wireless, visual, artificial intelligence (AI), and related technologies. The company engages in the design and development of technologies that enable connected in a range of communications and entertainment products and services, which are licensed to companies providing various products and services, including makers of wireless communications devices, consumer electronics, IoT devices, and cars and other motor vehicles, as well as providers of cloud-based services, such as video streaming. It designs and develops a range of innovations for use in digital cellular and wireless products and networks. The company also develops cellular technologies, such as technologies related to CDMA, TDMA, OFDM/OFDMA, and MIMO for use in 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G wireless networks, as well as mobile terminal devices; and 3GPP technology portfolio in 5G advanced and 6G, as well as technologies for mobile phones, automobiles and autonomous vehicles, wearables, smart factories and smart homes, robots, drones, and other connected consumer electronic products. In addition, it provides video coding and transmission technologies, and artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions. Further, the company's patented technologies are used in various products that include smartphones, tablets, consumer electronics, base stations, televisions, laptops, gaming consoles, set-top boxes, streaming devices, and connected automobiles, as well as patented technologies are used in various services, such as video streaming, user generated content sharing, video conferencing, video gaming, and other cloud-based services. InterDigital, Inc. was incorporated in 1972 and is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware.

financial_summary: InterDigital, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $7.3B market cap on $834M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 114% against a 9% cost of capital — a 104-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $529M in free cash flow — roughly 63 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.34× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 11.5×.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

Elevated short interest (12.8% of float) — sophisticated money is betting the other way

Technology sector lagging the market significantly, underperforming by 7% over 3 months
Elevated sector volatility (35% annualized) adds uncertainty

AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sect: Its 55% operating margin runs 48pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.36x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+31.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 10% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 26% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 0.93, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.53 vs 5y 0.90), so read it loosely.
About $58.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 47% in the 2020 crash, 44% in the 2022 bear market and 40% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 22% below its DCF fair value of $367, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 16%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $292 to $473 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/FCF 13.9 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 8% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 7.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $463 on average, 62% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 114% clears the cost of capital of 9.3% by 104pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.86).
It converts 63% of revenue into free cash flow, or 58% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.34x.
ROE of 37% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 19pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 40.5% of revenue on R&D and 5.2% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $768.5M (10% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 22.1% over 3 years, 18.4% over 5 years and 6.6% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 41%).
At current returns, reinvesting 17% of profits supports about 19.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 28.4% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.11 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 2.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue down 8%.
Capex runs only 0.2x depreciation (1.9% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 77, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.7%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $2.6M sold).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (1.4% in buybacks and 1.1% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.4% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 15 consecutive years, raising it 7.1% a year over the last five.
Short interest is elevated at 12.8% of the float, 14.0 days to cover.
people: With about 460 employees, each generates about $1.8M of revenue, 4.9x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 5.1% a year.
That works out to $1.1M of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.5M (1x revenue per employee).
